title: Barcode Standards
objectives: Understand barcode standards via a real-life analogy
Distinguish EAN-13, UPC-A, ITF-14, Code 128, GS1-128, GS1 DataBar, PDF417, Aztec

sections.markdown:
**Think of barcode standards as different languages spoken by the same alphabet of bars + squares.**

A barcode is a way to encode data. Symbologies differ in: character set, density, error correction, orientation (1D linear vs 2D matrix), and industry adoption. Picking the right one is like picking the right ISO standard — one wrong choice + your entire supply chain speaks the wrong language.

- **EAN-13 / UPC-A** — retail POS at cash register.
- **ITF-14** — case-level shipping labels.
- **Code 128 / GS1-128** — warehouse + logistics; carries any AI.
- **GS1 DataBar** — coupons + perishables; smaller than EAN.
- **PDF417** — driving licenses, boarding passes.
- **Aztec** — transit tickets.
- **QR** — consumer + payments.
- **DataMatrix** — pharma + small parts.

**Why every Flutter app touching physical goods must speak multiple symbologies:** a retail app scans EAN + Code 128 + DataMatrix; a boarding-pass app needs PDF417 + Aztec; a warehouse app touches Code 128 + DataMatrix + GS1-128. `mobile_scanner` + Scandit + ML Kit all expose format filters — enable ONLY what you need.

**Barcode standards** are the specifications that define symbologies — how data is encoded into bars, spaces, modules, and the printing/scanning rules. Governed by ISO/IEC + industry consortia (GS1, AIM). Common symbologies each optimized for a use case: retail (EAN/UPC), logistics (Code 128), pharma (DataMatrix), consumer (QR), transit (Aztec), documents (PDF417), coupons (GS1 DataBar).
## Symbology cheat sheet

## When each wins

- **Retail cash register** — EAN-13 / UPC-A (fixed length, easy scan).
- **Case shipping label** — ITF-14 (large bars, tough to damage).
- **Full logistics detail** — Code 128 / GS1-128 (any AIs).
- **Pharma serialized** — DataMatrix (small, high error correction).
- **Consumer scan** — QR (native camera support).
- **Boarding pass** — PDF417 (dense, alphanumeric).
- **Transit ticket** — Aztec (compact + tolerant).
- **UPS logistics** — MaxiCode (concentric-circle finder).
## Multi-symbology scanner config
## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: Enabling every symbology.** Slower detection + false positives. Restrict to your use cases.
**Mistake 2: Assuming Code 128 = GS1-128.** GS1-128 is Code 128 with FNC1 identifier + GS1 element strings. Not all Code 128 codes are GS1.
**Mistake 3: Wrong print size.** EAN needs ≥ 80 % of nominal size for POS-scanner reliability.
**Mistake 4: Missing quiet zone.** Every symbology requires a blank area around the code; without it scanners fail.
**Mistake 5: Contrast below 4:1.** Print quality matters as much as symbology choice.
**Mistake 6: PDF417 for consumer marketing.** Dense; ugly; consumer doesn't recognize. Use QR.
**Mistake 7: Aztec on packaging.** Unusual + few scanners know it outside transit. Stick to established symbologies for your industry.
**Mistake 8: Symbology mismatch between print + scanner config.** A brand prints DataMatrix; the retailer's scanner only enables Code 128 → silent-fail at POS.
## Best practices
**1. Pick per use case** — don't over-standardize.
**2. Verify with ISO grading** — 15416 (1D) / 15415 (2D).
**3. Enable only needed formats** in scanner.
**4. Quiet zone + print size + contrast** rules honored.
**5. Multi-symbology fallback** — try Code 128 if GS1-128 parse fails.
**6. Analytics per symbology** — track scan-fail rates.
**7. Sunrise 2027 planning** — retail migrating to 2D on packaging.
**8. Fallback to typed entry** for damaged labels.
## Practice programs
**Practice 1 (Easy)** — Restrict scanner to EAN + Code 128; test detection speed.
**Practice 2 (Medium)** — Route by symbology to different handler functions.
**Practice 3 (Medium)** — Detect + parse GS1-128 (Code 128 + FNC1) with AI extraction.
**Practice 4 (Hard)** — Analytics + Firebase log per symbology + scan-fail rate.
**Practice 5 (Expert)** — Retail Sunrise 2027 dual-encoding: EAN-13 on packaging + DataMatrix carrying same GTIN + batch + expiry.
## Interview Q&A

**Q1: Why so many symbologies?**

**A:** Different physical + operational constraints. **Retail POS scanner** (fixed laser at checkout) needs a 1D EAN-13 that scans in a swipe. **Warehouse handheld** scans Code 128 case labels + DataMatrix on damaged pallets. **Consumer phone** wants QR (recognizable, native camera support). **Boarding pass printer** needs PDF417 (dense, tolerant). **Pharma pill blister** needs DataMatrix (small print). No single symbology is best at everything: EAN can't carry batch/lot; QR too big for pill blister; PDF417 too dense for consumer camera. Standards exist so each industry picks its right tool. **Sunrise 2027 aims to converge on 2D** (QR / DataMatrix) but retail's installed POS scanners take decades to fully migrate. Interviewer signal: knowing the trade-offs, not just the names.

**Q2: What's the difference between Code 128 and GS1-128?**

**A:** **Code 128** — general-purpose 1D symbology supporting full ASCII. Data structure = whatever you encode. **GS1-128** (formerly UCC/EAN-128) — a *subset use* of Code 128 that: (1) starts with a specific `FNC1` character in position 1; (2) encodes data as GS1 element strings (AI-prefixed values). **Every GS1-128 is a Code 128, but not every Code 128 is a GS1-128.** Scanners often return both under the same symbology enum; you must inspect the raw payload for the `FNC1` marker + first-2-digit AI pattern to know. **Also:** GS1-128 rules include specific character-set constraints + separator handling for variable-length AIs (GS 0x1D). **Interviewer signal:** knowing the encoding is a Code 128 CONVENTION, not a separate symbology.

**Q3: When would you pick PDF417 over QR?**

**A:** **PDF417 wins when:** (1) Consumer familiarity doesn't matter (driver's license, boarding pass, government document). (2) Very high alphanumeric density needed. (3) Narrow rectangular space available (fits on a driving-license strip). (4) Existing industry standard mandates it (AAMVA driver-license spec; IATA boarding pass Bar Coded Boarding Pass BCBP). (5) Compression via variable rows + columns is useful. **QR wins for:** consumer marketing, payments, easy phone scan. **In practice:** you rarely 'choose' PDF417 for a green-field project; you use it because a downstream regulator or partner requires it. Interviewer signal: recognizing PDF417 = 'government / travel' domain.

**Q4: How do you architect a retail app that scans multiple symbologies?**

**A:** **(1) Symbology filter** — enable EAN-8/13, UPC-A/E, Code 128, GS1 DataBar (retail-common); reserve DataMatrix / QR for consumer-facing rollout. **(2) Router by format** — switch on `barcode.format` → EAN → GTIN lookup; Code 128 → check for FNC1 + parse as GS1-128; QR → check for Digital Link URL. **(3) Multi-format scanner** — `mobile_scanner` with formats list; Scandit for damaged codes. **(4) Fallback** — if no format matches, try typed entry. **(5) Analytics** — track scan-attempt vs scan-success per format; drops indicate label quality issue. **(6) Migration plan** — as retailers deploy 2D readers (Sunrise 2027), enable DataMatrix + QR reading + parse for Digital Link URLs carrying GTIN + batch + expiry. **(7) Regional variation** — India retail heavily EAN-13; US retail UPC-A + moving to 2D.

**Q5: What are the ISO grading standards for barcode print quality?**

**A:** **ISO/IEC 15416** — 1D barcode print quality (EAN, UPC, Code 128, etc.). Grades A (best) to F (fail); measures reflectance profile, decode + edge determination, symbol contrast. **ISO/IEC 15415** — 2D matrix symbols (DataMatrix, QR). Measures unused error correction, modulation, axial/grid non-uniformity, print growth. **Verifiers** — hardware devices (Cognex DataMan, Axicon) certified against these standards; grade every printed code. **Retail + regulatory require grade C or better.** **App-side:** if you're building a mobile print-quality checker, camera-based grade estimation gives a rough approximation; hardware verifier for authoritative grade. **Why bother:** grade-C+ codes have 99 %+ scan success in real world; grade-D drops to ~85 %. On a warehouse with 100 K scans / day, that's 15 K scan failures = worker frustration + errors.

**Q6: Sunrise 2027 — what changes + what's the migration?**

**A:** **Sunrise 2027** is the retail industry's commitment to have POS scanners capable of reading 2D codes (QR + DataMatrix) alongside classic 1D by end of 2027. Purpose: enable brand owners to encode more information (GTIN + batch + expiry + serial + Digital Link URL) on consumer packaging using one 2D code instead of a cluttered strip of 1D + text. **Migration:** (1) **Retailers** deploy 2D-capable scanners (imagers replace lasers). (2) **Brand owners** print DUAL-encoded barcodes on packaging (EAN-13 for legacy scanners + DataMatrix / QR carrying full Digital Link for new). (3) **Regulators** align on Digital Link URLs as machine-readable spec. (4) **Consumers** benefit from tap-to-scan getting rich product info. **App impact:** every retail app must be ready to parse Digital Link URLs from scanned QR / DataMatrix, in addition to legacy EAN. Not a hard deadline but the industry is moving fast. Interviewer signal: knowing this is happening + why.

## Real-world usage

- **Retail POS** — EAN-13 / UPC-A.
- **Case shipping** — ITF-14 / Code 128 / GS1-128.
- **Pharma** — DataMatrix.
- **Consumer marketing / payments** — QR.
- **Boarding passes / licenses** — PDF417 + Aztec.
- **Coupons / produce** — GS1 DataBar.
- **NOT ideal for** — over-standardizing on one; each has its lane.

## Advanced notes

- **AIM Symbology Identifiers** — scanner-returned prefix like `]C0` (Code 128), `]E0` (EAN-13), `]d2` (DataMatrix + GS1).
- **Sunrise 2027** — retail industry 2D migration.
- **RSS Symbology** — old name for GS1 DataBar.
- **GS1 Composite Symbology** — 1D + 2D stacked (retail coupon).
- **PDF417 macro** — split large payloads into multiple codes.
- **BCBP (IATA)** — Bar Coded Boarding Pass; PDF417 spec.
- **AAMVA** — driver-license PDF417 spec.
- **EMVCo QR** — merchant + consumer-presented payment QR global spec.
- **Symbol-quality analyzers** — Axicon, Cognex, HP Scanner Utility.
- **ISO 15420** — EAN + UPC symbology spec.
- **ISO 15417** — Code 128.
- **ISO 15438** — PDF417.
- **Multi-symbology decoders** — ZXing (open-source), ZBar, ML Kit, Scandit all handle diverse formats.
